orientation: A 120-assignment optional-editor campaign yielded 100 automatic ties and 20 changed-output reviews split 10/10. A post-review audit found only two unique answer pairs repeated ten times each, so the raw judgments are pseudoreplicated and cannot establish equal quality or justify promotion.
finding: The campaign validated tie filtering and self-matching but was inconclusive on editor quality because deterministic repetition collapsed the manual review to two unique comparisons.
limitations: Twenty manual judgments represented only two unique unordered answer sets.
The result reflects one owner's repeated judgments and deterministic temperature-zero outputs.
Private candidate text prevents public pair-level reanalysis.
negative_evidence: Optional editing achieved protocol success in only 60 of 120 trials.
The nominal 10/10 split cannot be interpreted as twenty independent comparisons.
The disposition rejects promotion or fine-tuning.
evidence_quotes: The raw manual aggregate was 10 direct-rewrite preferences, 10 optional-editor preferences, and no selected ties.
The repeated judgments provide a limited intra-rater consistency signal, not twenty independent quality comparisons.
Do not use the 10/10 raw aggregate as evidence of equal arm quality.
Do not promote or fine-tune from this campaign.
